name: Check TV channels

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: "17 5 * * *"
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  issues: write

concurrency:
  group: channel-check
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20

    steps:
      - name: Check out repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 24

      - name: Check every channel
        id: check
        run: node scripts/check-channels.mjs

      - name: Keep one issue up to date
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          FAILING: ${{ steps.check.outputs.failing }}
          TITLE: TV channels not playing
        run: |
          number=$(gh issue list --state open --search "in:title \"$TITLE\"" --json number --jq '.[0].number // empty')
          if [ "$FAILING" -gt 0 ]; then
            if [ -n "$number" ]; then
              gh issue edit "$number" --body-file channel-report.md
            else
              gh issue create --title "$TITLE" --body-file channel-report.md
            fi
          elif [ -n "$number" ]; then
            gh issue close "$number" --comment "Every channel is playing again."
          fi

name: Deploy GitHub Pages

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  # Rebuilds with a fresh TV guide. The free listings only look five or six hours ahead.
  schedule:
    - cron: "0 */4 * * *"
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: write

concurrency:
  group: github-pages
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  deploy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - name: Check out repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 24
          cache: npm

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Run tests
        run: npm test

      - name: Fetch the TV guide
        continue-on-error: true
        run: node scripts/build-tv-guide.mjs

      - name: Build GitHub Pages bundle
        run: npm run build:gh

      - name: Deploy to gh-pages
        uses: peaceiris/actions-gh-pages@v4
        with:
          github_token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          publish_dir: ./dist
          force_orphan: true

# Contributing

Thanks for taking a look.

This repo is a portfolio OS and aims to stay **GitHub Pages friendly** (client-only).

## Setup

```bash
npm install
```

## Dev

```bash
npm run dev
```

## Tests

```bash
npm test
```

## Build

```bash
npm run build
```

## GitHub Pages build

```bash
npm run build:gh
npm run deploy:gh
```

## Code standards (quick)

- Keep changes focused (small PRs / small commits).
- Prefer existing patterns in `src/components/shell/`, `src/stores/`, and `src/lib/`.
- Avoid adding server dependencies (the demo must work on static hosting).
- Add/adjust tests when changing core behaviors (filesystem, window manager, search).

# Taaniel OS A desktop operating system that runs in your browser, built as the portfolio of Taaniel Vananurm. Files are real files on a virtual disk, windows snap and move between desktops, and the big apps use real engines: Python, a Linux kernel, Doom and the Monaco editor. There is no server and no account. It all runs on GitHub Pages. **[Try it live](https://taan1el.github.io/taaniel-portfolio-os/)** · [Quick portfolio](https://taan1el.github.io/taaniel-portfolio-os/portfolio/) · [Download CV](https://taan1el.github.io/taaniel-portfolio-os/assets/CV_Taaniel_Vananurm_EN.pdf)

## What's inside | | | | --- | --- | | | | | **Projects** opens like a briefcase, with a pocket for each project | **Code** opens this repo's own source in Monaco, with tabs, search, diffs and a live preview | | | | | **Terminal** has two hand-written shells, plus real Python | **Contact** is an inbox with one-click email, phone and CV | | | | | **TV & Radio** has 88 live channels from Estonia, the UK and the USA, plus ERR radio and what's on now | **Doom** runs as WebAssembly | | | | | **Spreadsheet** has its own formula engine, with no eval | **Chess** knows every rule and plays back | Also on board: - **File Explorer** with tabs, a preview pane, Properties, drag and drop, shortcuts and a Recycle Bin - **Windows** with Snap Layouts, virtual desktops, Task View, a Task Manager and a Run dialog - **Linux** running on an x86 emulator - **Settings** with search, accent colours, clock formats, do not disturb and default apps - **Documents, Spreadsheet, Whiteboard and Calendar** - **Notepad, Notes, Paint, Calculator, Photos, Music and Video** - **Games**: Doom, Next Stop, Chess, Sudoku, Checkers, Solitaire, Dino, Hextris, Snake and Tetris ## Run it yourself ```bash npm install npm run dev ``` | Command | What it does | | --- | --- | | `npm test` | Runs the tests | | `npm run build` | Builds for production | | `npm run deploy:gh` | Builds and publishes to GitHub Pages | ## Built with - **App:** React 19, TypeScript, Vite, Zustand - **Motion and windows:** Framer Motion, GSAP, react-rnd - **Apps:** Monaco, xterm.js, pdf.js, hls.js - **Engines:** Pyodide (Python), v86 (Linux), Doom as WebAssembly. These download only when an app needs them. ## Project layout | Folder | What's there | | --- | --- | | `src/components/shell` | Desktop, Start menu, taskbar and windows | | `src/components/apps` | Every app | | `src/stores` | App state | | `src/lib` | Filesystem, shells, search and helpers | | `src/data` | Portfolio content and the starting files | ## Good to know - **Your data stays with you.** Everything you change is saved in your own browser. Use Start > Power > Reset this PC to clear it. - **The Browser app is an iframe.** Many sites refuse to load inside one, so it offers to open them in a new tab instead. - **TV streams come straight from each broadcaster.** Some programmes have no web rights, and some channels only open in their own country. - **Two scheduled jobs look after TV.** One flags channels that stop playing in a GitHub issue. The other refreshes what's on now from public listings. A channel with no listing shows no programme name. ## More docs [Architecture](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) · [Roadmap](docs/ROADMAP.md) · [Adding an app](docs/ADDING_AN_APP.md) · [Performance](docs/PERFORMANCE.md) · [Releasing](docs/RELEASE.md) · [Maintenance](docs/MAINTENANCE.md) · [Next Stop](docs/next-stop.md) · [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md)

# Adding an app

This OS uses a central app registry so apps can be discovered in the Start menu and launched consistently.

## 1) Create the app component

Add a new file in:

- `src/components/apps/<your-app>-app.tsx`

App components receive `AppComponentProps`:

- `window.id`, `window.title`
- `window.payload` (optional)

Most apps use:

- `AppScaffold`, `AppToolbar`, `AppContent`, `AppFooter` from `src/components/apps/app-layout.tsx`

## 2) Register the app

Edit:

- `src/lib/app-registry.tsx`

Add a new `defineApp({ ... })` entry with:

- `id`: unique string
- `title`, `description`, `category`
- `icon`: a `lucide-react` icon
- `defaultSize`: default window size
- `load`: lazy import pointing to your component

## 3) (Optional) Add a desktop shortcut

The desktop is the `/Desktop` folder (shown as `C:\Users\Taaniel\Desktop`), exactly as in Windows. Every icon is a file, folder or `.lnk` shortcut in it, and File Explorer's Desktop folder lists the same items. The only extra icon is the Recycle Bin, which is a system icon, not a file.

Edit:

- `src/data/desktop-seed.ts`

Add a row to `desktopShortcutSeeds`:

- `name`: the stored file name, ending in `.lnk` (`"Notes.lnk"`). The desktop hides the `.lnk`, so the label is `Notes`.
- `target`: `{ type: "app", appId }` for an app, `{ type: "path", path }` for a file or folder, or `{ type: "route", route }` for a page of this site
- `legacyId`: any unique string (it only matters for icon positions saved before the desktop was built from `/Desktop`)
- `defaultGridPosition`: the starting cell
- `since`: the new `DESKTOP_SEED_VERSION` (leave it out for a shortcut that ships with version 1)

Then bump `DESKTOP_SEED_VERSION`. Shortcuts are placed on the desktop once, recorded by a version marker on the `/Desktop` folder, so a visitor who deleted one never sees it come back by itself. Bumping the version adds only the new rows, to new and returning visitors alike, and never overwrites a file with the same name. Visitors can move, rename and delete shortcuts like any other file; the Recycle Bin and Start → Reset session bring them back.

## 4) (Optional) Associate files with your app

Edit:

- `src/lib/file-registry.ts`

Add extensions/mime-types to the file association map so a file opens in your app.

## 5) Test quickly

- `npm run dev` and launch the app from the Start menu.
- If the app uses filesystem nodes, verify it behaves in a persisted session and after “Reset session”.

## 6) Overlays, drag and drop and questions

- Files are dragged with pointer events (`src/lib/dnd`), and what is under the pointer decides where a drop lands. A panel that floats over the desktop (a flyout, a popover, a dialog) must carry the `w11-flyout` class or a `data-dnd-barrier` attribute, or a file dropped on it would fall through to the desktop behind it.
- To make something a drop target, spread `folderDropProps(path)` (a folder), `windowDropProps` (an app window) or `appDropProps` (an icon that runs an app) onto it.
- Ask "Are you sure?" with `confirmInOs` from `src/stores/confirm-dialog-store.ts`, not `window.confirm`: the shell shows its own dialog, and the browser's is silently answered "no" where dialogs are blocked.
- Code that deletes or moves files and reports errors itself (the terminal) should ask `getChangeRefusal(nodes, path)` from `src/lib/filesystem.ts` first, or call `tryDeleteNode` / `tryPasteNode` on the file system store, which say why nothing happened.

# Architecture

This repo is a browser-based desktop OS portfolio built with **React + TypeScript**. It runs entirely client-side (GitHub Pages compatible).

## High-level layers

- **Shell**: desktop surface, Start menu, taskbar, window host  
  `src/components/shell/`
- **Apps**: windowed applications (Files, Photos, PDF, Music, etc.)  
  `src/components/apps/`
- **State**: Zustand stores for shell/windows/processes/filesystem/system  
  `src/stores/`
- **Core logic**: filesystem helpers, launchers, search index, registries  
  `src/lib/`
- **Content + seeding**: portfolio copy, themes, bundled assets, seeded filesystem  
  `src/data/`

## Runtime flow

1. **Routing**: `/portfolio` renders the recruiter view, `/` renders the OS shell.  
   `src/app/App.tsx`
2. **Shell boot**: initializes filesystem + shell session state, then renders desktop + windows + overlays.  
   `src/components/shell/desktop-shell.tsx`
3. **Apps** are launched via a central `launchApp(...)` call with optional payload.

## Window manager

- Windows are draggable/resizable and keep z-order and focus.
- Window chrome lives in:  
  `src/components/shell/window-frame.tsx`
- The window host renders processes/windows:  
  `src/components/shell/window-host.tsx`

## App registry

Apps are defined in one place with metadata (title, icon, default size, category) and lazy-loaded implementations.

- `src/lib/app-registry.tsx`

This keeps the Start menu and launch logic consistent.

## Virtual filesystem + persistence

The filesystem is a virtual tree stored in memory and persisted to IndexedDB.

- Seeded nodes: `src/data/seedFileSystem.ts`
- Bundled assets: `src/data/bundled-assets.ts`
- Persistence and node operations: `src/stores/filesystem-store.ts`, `src/lib/filesystem.ts`

### Seed vs user files

- **Bundled/readonly** nodes are refreshed/migrated so older persisted sessions get updated asset paths.
- **User files** are stored in IndexedDB and survive reloads until “Reset session”.

## Search

- Start menu search uses an index built from apps and filesystem nodes.  
  `src/lib/shell-search.ts`
- An optional in-browser semantic reranker is included (Transformers + ONNX WASM).

## Known constraints

- Browser app is iframe-based; some sites block embedding via CSP/X-Frame-Options.
- Everything is static + client-side for GitHub Pages compatibility.

## Browser design

The Browser app is intentionally an iframe-based web viewer, not a full browser engine.

- **Why iframe is used**: it keeps the app lightweight, GitHub Pages-safe, and aligned with the rest of the OS window system. It also lets the Browser show local filesystem content through `srcDoc` without adding a server runtime.
- **Why some sites fail**: many third-party sites send `X-Frame-Options` or `Content-Security-Policy` headers that forbid embedding. Auth-heavy pages and complex web apps also tend to break inside iframe sandboxes. When that happens, the Browser shows a fallback panel instead of pretending the page loaded.
- **What the proxy does**: `Direct` loads the page as-is. `AllOrigins` and `Wayback` wrap the URL through external services that can sometimes return a frameable copy or archived snapshot. They are viewing aids, not a guarantee.
- **Tradeoffs**: this approach is honest and predictable, but it is not a replacement for Chrome. Some pages will render, some will need a proxy, and some should always be opened in a new tab.

# Portfolio maintenance

## 2026-11-01 (later)

Completed:
- Virtual x86: 9p now works, so `/mnt` is mounted and a Shared folder panel moves files both ways. The guest screen
  fills the window and scales to fit.
- TV: the picture has the whole stage with controls on top of it. Each tuning gets a new media element, so nothing of
  the last channel's playback can carry over. Changing channel also closes and reopens picture in picture.
- Code: rebuilt with a menu bar, breadcrumbs, minimap, Problems panel and Source Control. It opens this repo.

### Code's project

`scripts/build-project-source.mjs` packs every tracked file into `public/project-source.json`, which is not in git.
Text comes with its content, and binaries and the lockfile are listed read-only so the tree matches the repo. It runs in `dev`, `build` and `build:gh`, and Code fetches it only when opened. Edits stay in the visitor's browser. Monaco
still comes from its CDN, so the editor needs a connection. TypeScript checks syntax only, since the packages the source
imports are not in the editor.

## 2026-11-01

Completed:
- Phone taskbar: running apps scroll instead of sliding under the tray.
- English CV PDF for English visitors, with a test that keeps its facts in line with the Estonian one.
- New apps: Sudoku, Checkers, Solitaire, Chess, Task Manager, Whiteboard, Calendar, Spreadsheet and Documents.
- Run dialog, Paint undo and redo. File Explorer gained Properties, a preview pane and tabs.
- TV: a daily channel check and a what's on now guide.
- 406 lines of old Start menu CSS removed. Screenshots of Start were byte-identical before and after.
- First-load speed measured in `docs/PERFORMANCE.md`. The Run dialog now loads when opened.

### Scheduled jobs

- **Check TV channels** (`.github/workflows/channel-check.yml`) runs daily. It walks each stream to a real
  video segment, and retries failures after 90 seconds. It keeps one issue, "TV channels not playing", up to date, and
  closes it when every channel is back. Removing a channel stays a person's decision.
- A channel that answers 401, 403 or 451 is listed as refused, not dead, and does not open an issue by itself. The
  runner is in the USA, and region locking looks just like this. So a region-locked channel that really dies stays hidden
  until someone reads the report.
- **Deploy GitHub Pages** now also runs every four hours to rebuild `tv-guide.json`, which is not in git. The free
  listings mostly look only five or six hours ahead, so one run a day would leave the guide empty most of the day.
- GitHub turns off scheduled jobs after 60 days with no activity in the repo. Re-enable them on the Actions tab.

### TV guide sources

Telia's public guide for ETV, ETV2 and ETV+, and XMLTV from i.mjh.nz, epgshare01 and epg.pw for the UK and USA. None
of them promises to stay up, and Telia's is an unofficial endpoint. A source that fails is skipped, and its channels
show their category instead of a programme.

Names must match exactly within a region, so the wrong programme should not appear. Listings are for the same channel
on other services, so a regional schedule can still differ. Four channels were played and compared with their listing, and all four matched.

### Validation

- Figures for the final branch are in the pull request. Every app has a real-input Chromium check at desktop and 390px.
- Not tested on a physical phone, or with a real screen reader.
- `terminal-app-integration` ("opens a Command Prompt tab") failed once under load and passed 3 of 3 alone, so it is a
  known flaky test, not a fixed one.

## 2026-10-31

Completed:
- Code app: Monaco with tabs, quick open, search, a command palette and a live
  preview in a sandbox with no network access.
- Snap Layouts, virtual desktops and Task View.
- Bundled a Linux image for Virtual x86, and a self-hosted Pyodide in a worker
  behind the terminal's `python` command.
- Own canvas Dino and Hextris replace the paused ports. Next Stop is an app.
- Achievements, terminal extras, a Retro theme, and text size and contrast settings.
- Explorer: focus moves onto items so screen readers read them, and it stays in
  the window after the focused item goes away. Taskbar buttons take arrow keys.
- Start menu rebuilt: pins, Recommended, All by category, grid or list, account bar.
- Notepad replaces the Markdown viewer. New TV & Radio app with 88 channels and ERR radio (adds hls.js, gsap and @gsap/react).
- Settings grew six pages and a search box.
- Contact is an inbox, Projects is a briefcase. Popup tips and achievement toasts removed.
The CV has two sources, `docs/cv.html` (Estonian) and `docs/cv.en.html` (English). Print each to an A4 PDF in
`public/assets` after an edit; a test checks that both keep the same links, dates and numbers.

A changed shipped document only reaches returning visitors if the hash of its old
text is listed in `src/lib/portfolio-workspace.ts`. Add one whenever seed text changes.

### Validation

- `tsc`, 124 test files (1432 tests) and `build:gh` pass.
- Real-input Chromium runs pass for the desktop, windows, Code, the extras and
  the About, Projects, CV, Contact and case study path, plus a 390px phone.
- Not tested on a physical phone, or with a real screen reader.

## 2026-10-07

Completed:
- Moved PDF.js to the 6.x line; documents are torn down through the loading task.
- Updated Transformers, which pulls patched sharp, onnxruntime-node and adm-zip
  and drops the roarr/sprintf-js chain. No overrides or forced majors.
- Repaired the Browser's Wayback fallback (frame-friendly `2if_` snapshots) and
  stopped re-encoding addresses that were already normalized.

## 2026-09-09

- Verified Slow Pour against its static frontend and separate module-4 Express/SQLite source.
- Replaced campaign assets with public project screenshots; retained originals in an ignored local archive.

No major-version upgrades or application migrations. Vite stays on the 8.0 patch line.
DOMPurify hardens XML sanitization; Router and tooling updates include fixes.
Stricter sanitization can change previously accepted markup. Browser rendering and
the existing sanitization tests were checked after updating.

Release references:
- [DOMPurify 3.4.15](https://github.com/cure53/DOMPurify/releases/tag/3.4.15)
- [React Router 7.18.3](https://github.com/remix-run/react-router/releases/tag/react-router@7.18.3)

The local npm audit decreased from 17 findings (10 high) to 5 high findings.
This is a dependency report, not a claim that every advisory is reachable.

### Validation

- Node 24.14.1; versions read from package-lock.json.
- `npm test -- --maxWorkers=2`: 29 files, 128 tests passed.
- `npm run build` and `npm run build:gh`: TypeScript and production builds.
- No lint script exists; no claim of an ESLint pass.
- Recruiter route checked at 320, 390, 768 and 1440 pixels, including keyboard

### Backlog

[x] Review PDF.js 6 migration. Done 2026-10-07 (6.4.299); CI already runs Node 24.

[x] Track Transformers' Node-side sharp/onnxruntime-node/adm-zip advisories.
Done 2026-10-07: Transformers 4.3.1 depends on patched versions directly.

# Performance notes

This portfolio OS is designed to load quickly on static hosting (GitHub Pages).

## Strategy

- **Lazy-load apps**: most apps are loaded via dynamic import from the app registry (`src/lib/app-registry.tsx`).
- **On-demand workers**: the semantic search worker is only created when search query length is >= 3 (`src/hooks/use-shell-ai-search.ts`).
- **Separate entry points**: the desktop shell is dynamically imported, so opening `/portfolio` does not load the desktop or heavy app workers.
- **Static shell hosting**: the app runs client-side. Optional proxy modes and model downloads still depend on external services.

## Practical budget (targets)

- Fast first paint on the OS shell (desktop + Start menu usable quickly)
- Heavy apps (Monaco editor, pdf.js, v86) should not block initial interaction

## First-load measurements

Measured on 2026-11-01, before and after adding eleven apps and the File Explorer work
(`88e6fb4` against the release branch).

How: production builds under the Pages path, served locally with gzip, in headless
Chromium with the cache off. Each figure is the median of 7 cold visits, and each build
was measured twice. The lock screen is the first thing a visitor can use; its time
includes the short boot screen.

### First load, in bytes

| | Before | First attempt | Final |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Everything, gzipped | 299 KB | 346 KB | 308 KB |
| JavaScript, gzipped | 241 KB | 288 KB | 250 KB |
| Requests | 51 | 59 | 58 |

### Fast desktop, no throttling

| Median | Before | Final |
| --- | --- | --- |
| First contentful paint | 164–172 ms | 168 ms |
| Largest contentful paint | 2124–2140 ms | 2128–2132 ms |
| Lock screen ready | 2420 ms | 2417–2421 ms |
| Sign-in to desktop | 324–325 ms | 322–324 ms |

### Phone on 4G (390px, 20 Mbps, 40 ms, CPU slowed 4x)

| Median | Before | Final |
| --- | --- | --- |
| First contentful paint | 472–508 ms | 508–520 ms |
| Largest contentful paint | 1036–1256 ms | 1120–1124 ms |
| Lock screen ready | 2990–3004 ms | 3067–3069 ms |
| Sign-in to desktop | 359–372 ms | 312–384 ms |

### What changed

The first attempt added 47 KB of JavaScript. Nearly all of it was the terminal's command
tables, pulled into the first load by the Run dialog. Run now loads about four seconds after the desktop appears, or at once if it is asked for sooner, so it no longer competes with the first paint. The byte figures are taken at the lock screen, before that happens, so the visitor still downloads those 37 KB in the background.

The 9 KB left is real: the registry entries and icons for the new apps, which Start and
Search need straight away. The phone's lock screen came out about 70 ms slower in both
runs (2%), small enough that it may be noise but not proven so. The other timings overlap
with the first build's own run-to-run spread. The two measurements of each build are the
only samples, so read small differences with care.

## Tips for future optimizations

- Keep large optional apps hidden/collapsed in UX so recruiters hit the high-signal path first.
- Prefer moving rarely-used features behind explicit actions (open app, enable toggle) so they stay cold by default.
- If needed, split vendor chunks further in `vite.config.ts` using `manualChunks`.
- Anything the desktop shell imports directly lands on the first load. Check what a new dialog pulls in.

# What to add next

Everything here has to work on GitHub Pages: no server, no accounts. Size is rough:
S is an evening, M a few days, L a week or more. Icons and names are our own.

## Office

| App | Size | Plan |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Whiteboard | Done | Pan and zoom with pen, shapes and sticky notes, saved as a `.board` file. |
| Spreadsheet | Done | 28 functions on our own parser with no eval. Opens and saves `.csv`. Charts are still to come. |
| Documents | Done | Rich text with a strict allowlist, saved to the virtual disk, prints to PDF. |
| Presentation | M | Slides as data, a thumbnail rail, and a full-screen slideshow. |
| PDF Editor | L | Annotate, fill in and sign with `pdf-lib`, on top of the existing PDF viewer. |

## Collaboration

| App | Size | Plan |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Calendar | Done | Month view with local events, joined to the clock flyout. |
| Contacts | S | Address book stored locally, linked to Contact's Compose. |
| Signatures | S | Draw a signature and stamp it onto a PDF, all in the browser. Do after PDF Editor. |
| Email | Done | Contact is now an inbox. Real sending stays in the visitor's own mail app. |
| Team Chat | Skip | Real chat needs a server. A fake one with scripted people would not be honest. |
| Meetings | Skip | Video calls need a signalling server. Revisit if a backend ever exists. |

## Games

| Game | Size | Plan |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Sudoku | Done | Generator with a unique solution, three levels, pencil marks. |
| Checkers | Done | Rules engine with a small search AI. |
| Solitaire | Done | Klondike with drag and drop, undo, and auto-finish. |
| Chess | Done | Own rules engine, checked with perft, and a small AI in a worker. |
| Backgammon | M | Rules, dice and a basic AI. |
| BlockArena-style shooter | L | Single-player arena with bots in Three.js. Multiplayer needs a server. |

## The OS itself

| Feature | Size | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Task Manager | Done | Real windows, End task, frame rate and JS heap where the browser exposes it. |
| Run dialog | Done | `calc`, `cmd`, `notepad` and paths open the matching app. |
| Paint undo and redo | Done | Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Y. |
| Explorer Properties and preview pane | Done | Size, type, dates and location, plus a preview beside the list. |
| Explorer tabs | Done | Alt+T, Alt+W and Alt+1 to 9, because the browser keeps Ctrl+T and Ctrl+W. |
| Quiet notification history | M | A list in the clock flyout, nothing popping up. |
| Clipboard history | S | Remembers what was copied inside the OS. |
| Snipping tool | M | Region capture of the OS by redrawing it to a canvas. Cross-origin content stays blank. |
| Widgets board | M | Weather, a note and now-playing, using free no-key APIs. |
| System sounds | S | Sign-in and error sounds, off by default. |
| Cascade windows and side by side | S | In the taskbar menu. |

Alt+Tab and Windows-key shortcuts are mostly taken by the real OS before a web page
sees them, so these need their own keys, such as the existing Ctrl+Alt ones.

## TV & Radio

- **What's on now.** Done. The deploy job builds `tv-guide.json` from public listings.
- **Recheck the list.** Done. A daily job opens or updates one issue when a channel stops playing.
- **More listings.** 29 of the 88 channels have no match yet, so they show no programme. S each.
- **More countries.** Add channels only after playing each one over HTTPS from a browser. S each.

## Suggested order

1. Contacts and Clipboard history: small, and they join up what is already there.
2. Presentation, which completes the office apps.
3. Quiet notification history and the Widgets board.
4. PDF Editor, then Signatures.

# Next Stop minigame

Open **Games → Next Stop**, find **Next Stop** in Start/Search, or open `/Games/Next Stop.lnk` in File Explorer. Search also understands “steam train” and “railway”. The game is an original project by Taaniel, separate from the third-party ports that remain disabled.

The window embeds the local, MIT-licensed standalone HTML from `public/assets/games/next-stop/`. Its asset URL uses Vite's base path, including `/taaniel-portfolio-os/` for GitHub Pages. The bundled README records source commit, byte size and SHA-256. The game's renderer and dependencies stay out of the OS JavaScript bundle.

## Window behavior

- Switching windows pauses the player and stops the game's animation loop, including its title backdrop. Returning redraws the paused scene; the player chooses Resume.
- Minimizing unmounts apps in this OS. The adapter keeps that window's serialized journey in memory and restores it paused when the window returns. Indoor pose, cast/refill progress and other transient activities follow the game's normal save rules.
- Closing calls the game's destroy method to release graphics, listeners and audio. Reopening offers the game's saved local checkpoint through Continue last journey. Export/import JSON inside the game remains available.
- The game keeps its own sound controls. Their level is multiplied by the OS master volume; OS mute always silences it.
- Resize and maximize resize the iframe viewport. The game handles its normal resize event. Open full page offers the same local file in a separate tab.

WASD walks or adjusts power; E boards/delivers/leaves; Space brakes; B fires the boiler; J opens the journal; Esc pauses. Existing touch controls remain inside the game. First launch may take around a minute on a slow graphics driver. WebGL2 is required.

## Validation

`npm run test` includes adapter lifecycle/audio, search/shortcut integration and exact bundled-file checks. `npm run build` and `npm run build:gh` verify TypeScript and both asset bases. Browser QA should launch through Games, board/fire/drive, maximize, minimize/restore, switch to another app, close/reopen and continue a save. Inspect screenshots for the game inside the desktop frame. Unit tests do not substitute for WebGL drawing or real window interactions.

Checked on 30 October 2026 with Windows desktop Chromium 156.0.8078.4:

- Full Vitest suite: 105 files, 1,048 tests passed, including nine integration checks.
- Default production build and GitHub Pages build passed. Existing v86 externalization and large-chunk warnings remain.
- Actual browser inputs covered Games launch, boarding, firing, driving, braking, maximize, minimize/restore, switching to Calculator, returning paused, closing/reopening and continuing the saved journey. OS master mute held throughout. Screenshots of driving and restored/maximized views were inspected.
- The production preview launched and drew the game under `/taaniel-portfolio-os/assets/games/next-stop/next-stop.html`. Checked WebGL errors were zero, with no page errors in either browser run.
- The StrictMode regression was reproduced before its fix: an empty cleanup pass erased the minimized journey before the new iframe loaded. A component test now covers that restore and audio initialization on the first restored-frame gesture.

These are integration checks and a short drive, not a new complete railway circuit. Other browser families and physical mobile devices were not tested for this wrapper.

# Next Stop

Original rural railway game by Taaniel (Taan1el), distributed under the included MIT license.

- Source: https://github.com/Taan1el/next-stop
- Source commit: `282cfb6` (station-life review fixes)
- Bundled file: `next-stop.html`, 245,550 bytes
- SHA-256: `03cec70a0de995eb25ba95daa661ff3e65aec3ccca10b586a76c6540a40a832d`

This is an unchanged single-file build: numerical world data, direct glyph-cell WebGL2 renderer, inline UI and procedural Web Audio. No runtime images, game engines, network requests or companion files are required. The React shell loads it only when launched.

To update, copy a reviewed standalone build from the game repository, retain its license, and update this commit/checksum plus the asset assertion in `src/lib/games.test.ts`. Do not edit the bundled HTML separately from the game's source.

files.public/assets/v86/README.txt:
linux.iso is the small Linux image from the v86 project (https://github.com/copy/v86),
served at https://i.copy.sh/linux4.iso. The kernel and userland are GPL software;
see the v86 repository for how such images are built.

The image mounts the 9p device "host9p" at /mnt from /etc/profile, once for each of its two
login shells. The second mount always fails harmlessly, so the app clears that from the screen.

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 1920 1080" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice">
  <!--
    Dark Bloom: the night-time sibling of bloom.svg, drawn for this portfolio.
    Folded blue petals open from a glowing core right of centre, on a deep
    navy sky, so white desktop labels on the left stay easy to read.
  -->
  <defs>
    <radialGradient id="sky" cx="0.6" cy="0.62" r="0.75">
      <stop offset="0" stop-color="#0f2457" />
      <stop offset="0.45" stop-color="#071230" />
      <stop offset="1" stop-color="#02050e" />
    </radialGradient>

    <radialGradient id="halo" cx="0.5" cy="0.5" r="0.5">
      <stop offset="0" stop-color="#2f6bff" stop-opacity="0.55" />
      <stop offset="0.6" stop-color="#1238a8" stop-opacity="0.18" />
      <stop offset="1" stop-color="#0a1a4a" stop-opacity="0" />
    </radialGradient>

    <!-- petal fills run from the core (y=1) to the tip (y=0) -->
    <linearGradient id="back" x1="0" y1="1" x2="0" y2="0">
      <stop offset="0" stop-color="#06164a" />
      <stop offset="0.55" stop-color="#0f3497" />
      <stop offset="1" stop-color="#2a63e8" />
    </linearGradient>
    <linearGradient id="mid" x1="0" y1="1" x2="0" y2="0">
      <stop offset="0" stop-color="#0a2470" />
      <stop offset="0.5" stop-color="#1b55d6" />
      <stop offset="1" stop-color="#4d92ff" />
    </linearGradient>
    <linearGradient id="front" x1="0" y1="1" x2="0" y2="0">
      <stop offset="0" stop-color="#1340b0" />
      <stop offset="0.5" stop-color="#2f7cff" />
      <stop offset="1" stop-color="#9bd0ff" />
    </linearGradient>
    <linearGradient id="fold" x1="0" y1="0" x2="1" y2="0">
      <stop offset="0" stop-color="#ffffff" stop-opacity="0" />
      <stop offset="1" stop-color="#cfe6ff" stop-opacity="0.16" />
    </linearGradient>

    <radialGradient id="core" cx="0.5" cy="0.5" r="0.5">
      <stop offset="0" stop-color="#e8f4ff" />
      <stop offset="0.35" stop-color="#8cc6ff" stop-opacity="0.85" />
      <stop offset="1" stop-color="#2f6bff" stop-opacity="0" />
    </radialGradient>

    <!-- one petal: base at the origin, tip at (0,-1); scaled per layer -->
    <path id="petal" d="M0 0 C0.42 -0.28 0.36 -0.8 0 -1 C-0.36 -0.8 -0.42 -0.28 0 0 Z" />
    <path id="petal-fold" d="M0 0 C0.42 -0.28 0.36 -0.8 0 -1 Z" />

    <filter id="soft" x="-50%" y="-50%" width="200%" height="200%">
      <feGaussianBlur stdDeviation="60" />
    </filter>
    <filter id="glow" x="-50%" y="-50%" width="200%" height="200%">
      <feGaussianBlur stdDeviation="18" />
    </filter>
  </defs>

  <rect width="1920" height="1080" fill="url(#sky)" />

  <!-- halo behind the bloom -->
  <ellipse cx="1160" cy="640" rx="760" ry="560" fill="url(#halo)" />

  <g transform="translate(1160 790)">
    <!-- lower petals give the flower depth -->
    <g fill="url(#back)" stroke="#5f9bff" stroke-opacity="0.18" stroke-width="0.004" opacity="0.8">
      <use href="#petal" transform="rotate(-118) scale(330 300)" />
      <use href="#petal" transform="rotate(118) scale(330 300)" />
    </g>

    <!-- back layer -->
    <g fill="url(#back)" stroke="#6aa5ff" stroke-opacity="0.22" stroke-width="0.004">
      <use href="#petal" transform="rotate(-82) scale(520 560)" />
      <use href="#petal" transform="rotate(-41) scale(520 600)" />
      <use href="#petal" transform="rotate(0) scale(500 620)" />
      <use href="#petal" transform="rotate(41) scale(520 600)" />
      <use href="#petal" transform="rotate(82) scale(520 560)" />
    </g>
    <g fill="url(#fold)">
      <use href="#petal-fold" transform="rotate(-82) scale(520 560)" />
      <use href="#petal-fold" transform="rotate(-41) scale(520 600)" />
      <use href="#petal-fold" transform="rotate(0) scale(500 620)" />
      <use href="#petal-fold" transform="rotate(41) scale(520 600)" />
      <use href="#petal-fold" transform="rotate(82) scale(520 560)" />
    </g>

    <!-- middle layer -->
    <g fill="url(#mid)" stroke="#8cc0ff" stroke-opacity="0.26" stroke-width="0.004">
      <use href="#petal" transform="rotate(-62) scale(430 470)" />
      <use href="#petal" transform="rotate(-21) scale(430 500)" />
      <use href="#petal" transform="rotate(21) scale(430 500)" />
      <use href="#petal" transform="rotate(62) scale(430 470)" />
    </g>
    <g fill="url(#fold)">
      <use href="#petal-fold" transform="rotate(-62) scale(430 470)" />
      <use href="#petal-fold" transform="rotate(-21) scale(430 500)" />
      <use href="#petal-fold" transform="rotate(21) scale(430 500)" />
      <use href="#petal-fold" transform="rotate(62) scale(430 470)" />
    </g>

    <!-- front layer -->
    <g fill="url(#front)" stroke="#c4e2ff" stroke-opacity="0.3" stroke-width="0.004">
      <use href="#petal" transform="rotate(-40) scale(330 360)" />
      <use href="#petal" transform="rotate(0) scale(320 390)" />
      <use href="#petal" transform="rotate(40) scale(330 360)" />
    </g>
    <g fill="url(#fold)">
      <use href="#petal-fold" transform="rotate(-40) scale(330 360)" />
      <use href="#petal-fold" transform="rotate(0) scale(320 390)" />
      <use href="#petal-fold" transform="rotate(40) scale(330 360)" />
    </g>

    <!-- glowing core -->
    <ellipse cx="0" cy="-30" rx="150" ry="110" fill="#3d82ff" opacity="0.5" filter="url(#glow)" />
    <circle cx="0" cy="-24" r="90" fill="url(#core)" />
  </g>

  <!-- floor light so the bloom does not end in a hard edge -->
  <ellipse cx="1160" cy="960" rx="620" ry="150" fill="#123a9e" opacity="0.35" filter="url(#soft)" />
</svg>

import type { AppComponentProps, AppDefinition, AppId } from "@/types/system";

const componentCache = new Map<AppId, LazyExoticComponent<ComponentType<AppComponentProps>>>();

function defineApp(definition: AppDefinition): AppDefinition {
  return {
    minSize: { width: 320, height: 240 },
    resizable: true,
    mobileMaximized: true,
    ...definition,
  };
}

export function getAppRegistry() {
  return Object.values(registry).filter((app) => !app.hidden);
}

export function getAppDefinition(appId: AppId) {
  return registry[appId];
}

export function getAppComponent(appId: AppId) {
  const cachedComponent = componentCache.get(appId);

  if (cachedComponent) {
    return cachedComponent;
  }

  const component = lazy(registry[appId].load);
  componentCache.set(appId, component);
  return component;
}

export function canLaunchMultiple(appId: AppId) {
  return Boolean(registry[appId].multiple);
}

import { TERMINAL_SHORTCUTS } from "@/lib/terminal-keys";

/*
 * Reference text for the PowerShell tab: what Get-PSReadLineKeyHandler lists, and
 * (further down) what Get-Help knows beyond a command's synopsis. Plain data,
 * kept apart from the interpreter so it is easy to read and to check.
 */

export interface KeyHandler {
  key: string;
  function: string;
  description: string;
}

export interface KeyHandlerGroup {
  title: string;
  handlers: KeyHandler[];
}

/**
 * The keys the terminal's own line editor answers to, grouped the way
 * PSReadLine groups its functions. Only keys that really do something here
 * are listed; terminal-line.ts and terminal-session.ts handle them.
 */
export const READLINE_KEY_HANDLERS: KeyHandlerGroup[] = [
  {
    title: "Basic editing functions",
    handlers: [
      { key: "Enter", function: "AcceptLine", description: "Run the line" },
      { key: "Backspace", function: "BackwardDeleteChar", description: "Delete the character before the cursor" },
      { key: "Delete", function: "DeleteChar", description: "Delete the character under the cursor" },
      { key: "Ctrl+Backspace", function: "BackwardKillWord", description: "Delete the word before the cursor" },
      { key: "Ctrl+w", function: "BackwardKillWord", description: "Delete the word before the cursor" },
      { key: "Ctrl+Delete", function: "KillWord", description: "Delete the word after the cursor" },
      { key: "Ctrl+Home", function: "BackwardDeleteLine", description: "Delete from the start of the line to the cursor" },
      { key: "Ctrl+End", function: "ForwardDeleteLine", description: "Delete from the cursor to the end of the line" },
      { key: "Escape", function: "RevertLine", description: "Throw away what is typed on the line" },
      { key: "Ctrl+c", function: "CancelLine", description: "Cancel the line, or stop the command that is running" },
      { key: "Ctrl+l", function: "ClearScreen", description: "Clear the screen and keep the line" },
    ],
  },
  {
    title: "Cursor movement functions",
    handlers: [
      { key: "LeftArrow", function: "BackwardChar", description: "Move the cursor one character left" },
      { key: "RightArrow", function: "ForwardChar", description: "Move one character right; at the end of the line, take the grey suggestion" },
      { key: "Ctrl+LeftArrow", function: "BackwardWord", description: "Move the cursor to the start of the previous word" },
      { key: "Ctrl+RightArrow", function: "NextWord", description: "Move the cursor to the start of the next word" },
      { key: "Home", function: "BeginningOfLine", description: "Move the cursor to the start of the line" },
      { key: "Ctrl+a", function: "BeginningOfLine", description: "Move the cursor to the start of the line" },
      { key: "End", function: "EndOfLine", description: "Move to the end of the line; there, take the grey suggestion" },
      { key: "Ctrl+e", function: "EndOfLine", description: "Move the cursor to the end of the line" },
    ],
  },
  {
    title: "History functions",
    handlers: [
      { key: "UpArrow", function: "PreviousHistory", description: "Bring back the previous command" },
      { key: "DownArrow", function: "NextHistory", description: "Bring back the next command" },
      { key: "F8", function: "HistorySearchBackward", description: "Previous command that starts with what is typed" },
      { key: "Shift+F8", function: "HistorySearchForward", description: "Next command that starts with what is typed" },
    ],
  },
  {
    title: "Completion functions",
    handlers: [{ key: "Tab", function: "Complete", description: "Complete the command, parameter or path; list the choices when several fit" }],
  },
  {
    title: "Miscellaneous functions",
    handlers: [
      { key: "PageUp", function: "ScrollDisplayUp", description: "Scroll the screen up one page" },
      { key: "PageDown", function: "ScrollDisplayDown", description: "Scroll the screen down one page" },
      { key: "Ctrl+v", function: "Paste", description: "Paste from the clipboard (long or multi-line text asks first)" },
    ],
  },
  {
    title: "Terminal functions",
    handlers: TERMINAL_SHORTCUTS.map((shortcut) => ({
      key: shortcut.keys.join("+"),
      function: "Terminal",
      description: shortcut.label,
    })),
  },
];

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ examples

/** [what to type, what it does] */
export type HelpExample = [code: string, remarks: string];

/** Get-Help -Examples, keyed by the command's own name. Every example is something this shell runs. */
export const HELP_EXAMPLES: Record<string, HelpExample[]> = {

/** Case-insensitive lookup of one topic. */
export function findAboutTopic(name: string): AboutTopic | undefined {
  const wanted = name.toLowerCase();
  return ABOUT_TOPICS.find((topic) => topic.name.toLowerCase() === wanted);
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ parameters

export interface SyntaxParameter {
  name: string;
  /** The type or value set shown after the name ("<string[]>", "File|Directory"); null for a switch. */
  type: string | null;
}

/**
 * The parameters a command's syntax line shows: "-Path <string>" and "[-Recurse]".
 * Used for the PARAMETERS section of Get-Help and for completing a parameter name.
 */
export function syntaxParameters(syntax: string): SyntaxParameter[] {
  const found: SyntaxParameter[] = [];
  const pattern = /-([A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9]*)\]?(?:\s+(<[^>]+>|[A-Za-z]+(?:\|[A-Za-z]+)+))?/g;
  for (const match of syntax.matchAll(pattern)) {
    // "-gt" inside prose and a pipeline's own "|" are not parameters: a parameter follows [ or a space.
    const before = match.index > 0 ? syntax[match.index - 1] : " ";
    if (before !== "[" && before !== " " && before !== "|") continue;
    if (!found.some((entry) => entry.name.toLowerCase() === match[1].toLowerCase())) found.push({ name: match[1], type: match[2] ?? null });
  }
  return found;
}
